text:
Maya (Product): dropped a compact p95 card mock into Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE - wanted a quick sync on hover behavior + keyboard interactions.

Eli (Design): sketched two options: (A) right-anchored info overlay that keeps the timeline visible, (B) bottom sticky popover which works better on narrow widths. question: should the popover block scrubber interactions? i think no.

Sam (Frontend): prefer the overlay on desktop. for mobile, bottom popover is safer. implementation caveat: overlay needs a focus trap when opened via keyboard so screen reader users don't tab away.

Kai (Eng): agree on focus trap. propose a pattern: opening sets focus to first TABBABLE element in the panel; Esc closes and returns focus to trigger. also add `aria-modal=\"false\"` (not a true modal) and `role=\"dialog\"` for the panel.

Eli (Design): good call. microcopy: current hover line says \"p95 320ms (n=1,234)\" — Jordan, can we shorten?

Jordan (PM): shorten to: \"p95: 320 ms • n=1,234\" — keeps machine-parsable look and is scannable. For drill-through link use \"View raw traces\".

a11y-bot: auto-check: ensure 44x44px hit target on the scrubber thumb, provide visible focus ring (2-3px), supply `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` updated on thumb move. Announce popover open with `aria-live` or `role=status`.

Sam (Frontend): technical note: we'll lazy-load the extra metrics in the overlay after the first open to avoid inflating initial bundle. also, prefer CSS-only show/hide where possible to keep repaint cheap.

Eli (Design): color palette: switch heatmap to a colorblind-safe sequential ramp (Viridis or ColorBrewer YlGnBu). current red->yellow->green misleads for low->high mapping. update legend copy to state \"darker = more requests\" to avoid misreads.

Maya (Product): sampling control placement: two schools — global app-level default vs per-card control. leaning per-card with an org-wide default fallback. must be hidden under \"advanced\" to avoid UI noise.

Sam (Frontend): implement as per-card override in gear menu. default shown in header tooltip: \"Sampling: auto (override)\". gear menu should surface a short explanation.

Eli (Design): suggested gear tooltip text: \"Sampling rate — reduce to smooth noise; increase to surface short spikes\". Jordan prefers shorter.

Jordan (PM): cut to: \"Sampling — lower reduces noise\". Link to docs for examples.

Kai (Eng): backend can emit sample count and average latency per bucket; if we show sample count in hover (\"n=1,234\") it helps users judge confidence. cheap delta if metrics already instrumented.

Eli (Design): accessibility nit: ensure keyboard Left/Right moves the scrubber and that the scrubber value is read as \"time: 14:32:21, p95 320 ms\". Also add visible tooltip on focus (not just hover).

Sam (Frontend): will wire keyboard handlers and exposed aria attributes. question: should scrubber increments be fixed time deltas or adapt to zoom? prefer adaptive steps based on visible window.

Kai (Eng): adaptive stepping is better UX but slightly more complex; fine to do. server will return time buckets so client can snap to nearest bucket timestamp.

Eli (Design): legend decision: show 3 buckets on mobile, 5 buckets on desktop for nuance. also add a compact legend (small squares) with an accessible text label for screen readers.

Maya (Product): finalize next steps: Eli to update Figma with right-overlay + bottom popover responsive rules, colorblind palette, focus styles, and revised microcopy. Sam/Kai to prototype keyboard interactions and lazy-load pattern. Jordan to update docs copy. a11y-bot to run checklist after prototype.

Sam (Frontend): quick implement note: we should debounce scrubber keyboard events to avoid excessive tracing calls when moving quickly.

Eli (Design): pushed updated mock, flagged a11y points in-comments. linking to file in thread.

Maya (Product): thanks team — we'll review the prototype in next UX sync. closing thread.
